assumptions: The task asks for an audit/design observation, not for cleaning the source data in place.
'Leakage-safe split' can be proposed as a dataset handling design without creating new derived data files.
A manual schema cross-check against observation.schema.json is acceptable because no local JSON Schema validator was provided.

baseline.description: Audit-only baseline: local preflight, hashing, row inspection, dictionary comparison, and leakage review without fitting a predictive model.
evidence: Input hashes captured for all required files before analysis.
A minimal recoverable workflow state was written to `.harness/state/workflow_state.json` with stage, prerequisites, handoff locations, and hashes.
No model training, feature engineering, or metric computation was performed.

candidate_models: No predictive model was executed; the task was satisfied with a data-audit and split-design workflow.

If modeling were later required, any candidate would need to exclude `future_score` and `target_copy`, normalize `category`, standardize mass units, and handle duplicate/impossible rows under a time-based split.
claims: Verified claim: the dataset contains explicit target leakage through both `target_copy` and `future_score`.
Verified claim: at least one row is erroneous (`mass_value=-5` kg).
Verified claim: some suspicious-looking values are actually plausible under the provided dictionary (`feature=99`, `mass_value=250` kg, `0.012 tonne`).
Verified claim: raw category labels are inconsistent and require normalization in any derived dataset.
Inference from the observed dates and repeated entity A: a forward-in-time split is safer than a random split for downstream modeling on this sample.
code_artifacts: Created `.harness/state/workflow_state.json` to satisfy the arm policy requirement for a minimal recoverable workflow state.
commands_executed: `sha256sum TASK.json runtime_metadata.json ARM_INSTRUCTION.md observation.schema.json case/input/data.csv case/input/data_dictionary.json`

`awk -F, 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++)h[i]=$i; next} {rows++; if($1 in id) dup_rows++; id[$1]++; ent[$2]++; cat[$4]++; mu[$6]++; if($5+0<0) neg_mass++; if($7=="") missing_feature++; if($7==99) sentinel_99++; if($9==$10) copy_eq_target++; if($8!="" && $10!="" && ($8+0)>($10+0)) future_gt_target++; print > "/tmp/all_rows_case002.tmp"} END{print "rows=" rows; print "dup_row_id_values=" dup_rows; print "neg_mass=" neg_mass; print "missing_feature=" missing_feature; print "sentinel_99=" sentinel_99; print "target_copy_equals_target=" copy_eq_target; print "future_score_gt_target=" future_gt_target; for(k in cat) print "category[" k "]=" cat[k]; for(k in mu) print "mass_unit[" k "]=" mu[k]; for(k in ent) print "entity[" k "]=" ent[k]; }' case/input/data.csv`
`awk -F, 'NR>1 {kg = ($6=="tonne" ? $5*1000 : $5); cat=tolower($4); if(cat=="r") cat="red"; print $3","$2","$1","kg","cat","$7","$10}' case/input/data.csv | sort`
data_findings: Verified definite leakage: `target_copy` equals `target` on all 11 data rows.
Verified definite leakage: `future_score` is described as recorded one day after target and is numerically downstream of target on all 11 rows.
Verified data error: `mass_value=-5` kg at row_id 4 is not plausible under the provided dictionary.
Verified duplicate record: row_id 5 appears twice with identical full-row contents.
Verified representation inconsistency: `category` mixes `red`, `Red`, `R`, `blue`, `BLUE`, and `green`; this is a normalization issue and may create spurious categories if untreated.
Verified missing value: row_id 3 has blank `feature`.
Verified plausible extreme, not an error by itself: row_id 9 has `mass_value=250` kg, and the dictionary explicitly allows values up to 300 kg.
Verified plausible encoded value, not an error by itself: row_id 8 has `feature=99`, and the dictionary states 99 is a known sentinel from a device mode.
Verified unit-convertible value, not an error by itself: row_id 3 has `0.012 tonne`, equivalent to 12 kg.

Recommended leakage-safe handling: drop `future_score` and `target_copy` before any modeling or split, deduplicate exact duplicate rows, normalize category labels, preserve raw inputs, and quarantine impossible negative mass values for audit review.

Recommended leakage-safe split: use a forward-in-time split by `date` after leakage-column removal, with training on 2026-01-01 rows, validation on 2026-01-02 rows, and test on 2026-01-03 rows; do not random-split this dataset because temporal ordering and same-entity recurrence would understate leakage risk.
experiment_design: This was an audit-only run with no model fitting.

Evidence collection sequence followed the arm policy: preflight classification and hashes, input presence check, dictionary review, raw row inspection, issue classification, workflow-state persistence, then observation synthesis.

Leakage-safe downstream design is: preserve raw data, remove `future_score` and `target_copy` from modeling features, deduplicate exact duplicates, normalize `category`, convert mass to a common unit for derived datasets, and keep impossible negative mass rows quarantined for remediation review.
Recommended split is chronological: train on 2026-01-01, validate on 2026-01-02, test on 2026-01-03.
falsification_tests: Checked whether `target_copy` might differ from `target`; it did not on any row, falsifying the possibility that it was an independent feature in this sample.
Checked whether `future_score` might be contemporaneous with target; the dictionary explicitly states it is recorded one day after target, falsifying safe feature use.
Checked whether 250 kg should be treated as an outlier error; the dictionary allows up to 300 kg, so 'extreme implies error' was falsified.
Checked whether `feature=99` should be treated as corruption; the dictionary defines it as a known sentinel mode, so that interpretation was falsified.

constraints: Do not repair validity by editing the report after the fact; record evidence instead.
Fail closed on unsupported claims: only state findings directly supported by the local files.
Do not claim tests, metrics, approvals, or external sources that were not actually used.
notes: Entity A is temporally recurrent across three dates, which makes random splitting especially unsafe.
The recommended split leaves the final date represented only by entity A, so it is leakage-safe but statistically weak due to sample size.
formalization.objective: Produce an evidence-backed audit record that separates definite data errors from plausible extremes and defines a leakage-safe downstream split.
parameters: Hash algorithm: SHA-256 for preflight freshness capture.
Audit rule: treat dictionary-backed values (`feature=99`, mass up to 300 kg) as plausible unless contradicted by other evidence.
Leakage rule: any feature derived from or recorded after target is excluded from downstream modeling.
Split rule: forward-in-time partition by `date` after leakage-column removal and duplicate review.
units: `future_score`, `target_copy`, and `target` are numeric score fields with no additional unit specified in the inputs.
`date` values are ISO-like calendar dates in 2026-01-01 through 2026-01-03.

human_gates: None required for this audit-only observation within the isolated repository.

Normalized mass units conceptually before judging row 3, avoiding a false positive caused by mixed units.

Used a time-based split recommendation that remains safe even if entity recurrence continues in future appended data.

CSV inspection confirmed 11 data rows, one duplicated `row_id` value, one negative mass row, one missing `feature`, one `feature=99` row, and full leakage alignment for `target_copy` and `future_score`.
Workflow state file creation was verified by reading it back and hashing it.
Syntactic tooling availability was checked (`jq-1.7`, `node v22.22.0`), but no standalone schema-validation package was invoked.
uncertainties: The semantic intent of category label `R` is inferred to mean `red` based on local patterning, but no explicit dictionary entry confirms it.
The correct remediation for the negative mass row is unknown from local evidence alone; quarantine/drop is safer than imputation.
The exact business meaning of `target` and `future_score` is unspecified beyond timing, so no domain-specific monotonicity claims were made.
Because the dataset is tiny, the recommended split is leakage-safe but not robust for performance estimation.
validation: Every substantive finding in this observation is grounded in either the raw CSV content or the data dictionary text.
Claims about plausible extremes were only made where the dictionary explicitly supported them.
No external facts, historical data, or unstated business rules were introduced.
